title: Dealer Locator Test new
featureSummary: Verify the dealer locator page (search input, top-cities scroller, results page) renders and behaves correctly on a 360x600 mobile viewport.
conclusion: CRITICAL: the top-cities list exposes exactly 5 cities, but AC-4 explicitly requires more than 5 - confirmed in the live DOM twice, including a fresh-context recheck. Two further MAJOR defects were confirmed: dealer card addresses are CSS-truncated with an ellipsis on the results page (violates AC-3's 'no text truncation' requirement), and the 'Locate me' control - though it does become visually visible on input focus per AC-1 - permanently keeps tabindex="-1", so it can never be reached via keyboard Tab (the exact scenario asked about in the Jira comment). AC-1's overflow/visibility clauses and AC-2's scroller/tap-blocking clauses both passed.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: The dealer search input is fully visible and tappable at 360px width, with no horizontal overflow on the page. The "Locate me" control may be hidden until the search input is focused, but must become fully visible once focus occurs.

The top cities horizontal scroller is swipeable on mobile, and every city (Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York) can be scrolled into view and tapped - the fade gradient on the scroller's edges must not visually cover or block taps on the last visible city.
Selecting a city from mobile reaches the results page, and dealer cards stack in a single readable column with no text truncation or overlapping elements.
Dealer search page should have more than 5 cities.

commentScenarios.summary: Once the "Locate me" control becomes visible after focusing the search input, can it actually be reached and activated using only the keyboard (Tab, then Enter) - not just a mouse or touch tap?
commentScenarios.notes: Locate me stays tabindex="-1" permanently even after opacity goes 0->1 on focus, so pressing Tab from the input skips straight over it to the next real focusable control; reproduced in a fresh context.

scenarios.name: Dealer locator page loads at 360x600 with core elements rendered
steps: Navigate to /auto/dealer-locator on a 360x600 viewport
Dismiss the consent banner
Confirm hero title, productline dropdown, search input and top-cities list are all rendered
scenarios.expected: Page loads with all core dealer-locator widgets rendered, no blocking errors.
scenarios.actual: Header, hero title, search input and top-cities scroller all rendered correctly.

scenarios.name: Search input visible/tappable with no horizontal overflow; Locate me becomes visible on focus
steps: Measure document.scrollWidth vs window.innerWidth
Measure the search input's bounding rect against the 360px viewport
Click the search input and re-measure the Locate me button's opacity and viewport position
scenarios.expected: No horizontal overflow; input fully within the 360px viewport; Locate me becomes fully visible (opacity 1, within viewport bounds) once the input is focused.
scenarios.actual: scrollWidth === innerWidth === 360 (no overflow). Input rect: x=16, width=328 - fully inside the viewport. After focusing the input, Locate me's opacity went from 0 to 1 and its rect (x=24, width=312) is fully within the viewport.

scenarios.name: Top-cities scroller is swipeable and its edge fade gradients don't block or visually cover taps
steps: Inspect .dl__top-cities-list overflow-x and scrollWidth/clientWidth
Locate the .dl__top-cities--gradient-left/right overlay elements and read pointer-events/z-index/background
Scroll the list to its maximum scrollLeft and screenshot the last visible city under the gradient
scenarios.expected: The scroller is horizontally scrollable and the fade gradients do not visually cover or block taps on the last visible city.
scenarios.actual: overflowX:auto, scrollWidth 550 > clientWidth 328 (genuinely scrollable). Both gradient overlays have pointer-events:none, so they cannot intercept taps. The gradient's own color fades to the same navy background used by the page/pills, so the city name text stays fully legible in the screenshot even though its bounding box geometrically overlaps the gradient region.

scenarios.name: Top-cities list has more than 5 cities
steps: Query all .dl__top-cities-list a elements and count them
Repeat the count in a fresh browser context
scenarios.expected: More than 5 cities listed, per AC-4.
scenarios.actual: Exactly 5 cities (Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York) in both the original context and a fresh-context recheck.

scenarios.name: Autocomplete search end-to-end: type a city, select a suggestion, reach results
steps: Type "Atlan" into the search input
Read the autocomplete suggestion list
Click the "Atlanta, GA" suggestion
Wait for the results page to finish loading
scenarios.expected: Selecting a suggestion navigates to a results page showing dealer cards.
scenarios.actual: Suggestion list populated with Atlanta, GA / Atlantic City, NJ / etc. Clicking "Atlanta, GA" showed a loading state then landed on /auto/dealer-locator/atlanta,-ga with 20 dealer cards rendered.

scenarios.name: Results page: single-column card stacking, no overlap, no text truncation
steps: Load the New York results page
Measure each dealer card's bounding rect to confirm no vertical overlap between consecutive cards
Measure each .dl__card-dealer__address-direction-text span's scrollWidth vs clientWidth
scenarios.expected: Cards stack in a single readable column with no overlapping elements and no truncated text, per AC-3.
scenarios.actual: Cards stack correctly in a single column with zero overlap detected across 6 sampled cards. However every sampled address span (8/8) has white-space:nowrap, text-overflow:ellipsis and a fixed 270px width, and scrollWidth consistently exceeds clientWidth (e.g. 352px content in a 270px box) - the address is visibly cut off with an ellipsis. Reproduced identically in a fresh context.

scenarios.name: Mobile hamburger navigation opens and closes
steps: Click the header's icon button (hamburger)
Confirm a nav/dialog element becomes visible
Click the same button again to close it
scenarios.expected: The mobile nav opens and closes on tap.
scenarios.actual: A '.ds__nav' element became visible after the first click; the same control closed it again on a second click.

scenarios.name: Chat assistant widget ("Mitch"/Virtual tire expert) opens
steps: Click the "Chat with us" floating launcher button
Confirm the chat panel renders
scenarios.expected: The chat launcher opens the assistant panel (third-party embed - opened only, internals not driven further, per standing constraints).
scenarios.actual: The 'Virtual tire expert' panel opened with quick-reply chips (Tire Specs, Tire Warranty, Motorcycle Tires, Bicycle Tires) and a text input, rendered correctly.

scenarios.name: Boundary: invalid/nonsense search input is handled gracefully
steps: Type "zzzznotarealcity12345" into the search input
Confirm no crash and no spurious suggestion results
scenarios.expected: Natural graceful handling of an implausible query - no crash, no console error, no injected results.
scenarios.actual: 0 city suggestions returned, only the "Locate me" option remained in the dropdown; no crash, no new console errors attributable to the input.

scenarios.name: Keyboard reachability of "Locate me" once visible (comment scenario)
steps: Focus the search input (Locate me becomes visually visible)
Press Tab
Read document.activeElement and the Locate me button's tabindex attribute
Repeat in a fresh browser context
scenarios.expected: Once visible, Locate me should be reachable via Tab and activatable with Enter.
scenarios.actual: Tab moves focus straight to the next 'ds__btn' anchor, never landing on Locate me. Its tabindex attribute is permanently "-1" even after opacity goes 0->1 on focus. Reproduced identically in a fresh context.

scenarios.name: Boundary: clearing the search input restores the original state
steps: Type "Dallas" into the search input
Clear the input
Confirm the input value is empty and the top-cities list is present again
scenarios.expected: Clearing the input restores the exact original state.
scenarios.actual: Input value returned to "" and the top-cities list (5 links) was present and unchanged.

scenarios.name: Boundary: back button after selecting a city restores the search page
steps: From the Atlanta results page, trigger the browser back button
Confirm the search input and top-cities list are present again
scenarios.expected: Back button restores the dealer-locator search page gracefully.
scenarios.actual: Landed back on /auto/dealer-locator with the search input present and 5 top-cities links intact.

scenarios.name: TC-AN1 - analytics fires on navigation
steps: Snapshot window.dataLayer length before navigating
Click a footer link to navigate to a new page
Compare dataLayer length and capture analytics network requests
scenarios.expected: At least one analytics request or dataLayer push captured after an interaction.
scenarios.actual: window.dataLayer grew to 31 entries and multiple googleads.g.doubleclick.net/pagead/viewthroughconversion requests fired for both the dealer-locator and destination page views.

scenarios.name: Footer link grid renders and navigates
steps: Scroll to the bottom of the page
Identify the visible (non-hidden) footer link grid
Click the "Accessibility Statement" link and confirm navigation
scenarios.expected: The footer link grid renders and at least one link navigates correctly.
scenarios.actual: Navigated successfully to /accessibility-statement. Note: the DOM also contains a separate, entirely visibility:hidden duplicate footer/subnav tree with the same links - only the visible one is used, no functional impact.

bugs.title: Dealer card address text is truncated with an ellipsis on the results page - AC-3 not fully met
steps: Load a dealer results page at 360x600
Read each .dl__card-dealer__address-direction-text span's computed style and scrollWidth/clientWidth
Repeat in a fresh browser context
bugs.expected: Dealer card addresses display with no text truncation, per AC-3.
bugs.actual: Every sampled address span (8/8, e.g. "396-420 MARIN BLVD, New Jersey, JERSEY CITY - 07302") has white-space:nowrap, text-overflow:ellipsis and a fixed 270px width; scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth in every case (e.g. 352px vs 270px). Reproduced identically in a fresh context.
bugs.impact: Mobile users at 360px width cannot read the full street address on a dealer card without opening the "See map"/directions link - a workaround exists, but the AC's explicit "no text truncation" requirement is not met.

bugs.title: "Locate me" control cannot be reached via keyboard Tab even after becoming visible on focus
steps: Focus the search input (Locate me opacity goes 0 -> 1)
Press Tab
Read document.activeElement and Locate me's tabindex attribute
Repeat in a fresh browser context
bugs.expected: Once visually visible, Locate me should receive focus via Tab and be activatable with Enter, per the Jira comment scenario.
bugs.actual: Tab moves focus past Locate me directly to the next real focusable element; Locate me's tabindex attribute is permanently "-1" regardless of its visibility state. Reproduced identically in a fresh context - this is a DOM attribute value, not an inference.
bugs.impact: Keyboard-only users can never activate the geolocation shortcut, even though it is visually present - a real accessibility gap on a control the page itself makes visible for exactly this purpose.

bugs.title: Top-cities list exposes only 5 cities - AC-4 requires more than 5
steps: Load the dealer locator page at 360x600
Query all .dl__top-cities-list a elements and count them
Repeat in a fresh browser context
bugs.expected: More than 5 cities listed, per AC-4.
bugs.actual: Exactly 5 cities (Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York) in both the original run and a fresh-context recheck - a DOM element count, not an inference.
bugs.impact: The literal, testable acceptance criterion ("more than 5 cities") is not met at all - there is no ambiguity in this failure.

automationGap.recommendation: The top-cities count (AC-4) is already expressible with the existing 'I should see more than {int} "top cities"' step and the registered 'top cities' collection - it just needs to be added as a scenario; it would fail today and codify the CRITICAL gap. Keyboard-focus assertions and truncation checks are the two real vocabulary gaps: a small focus-assertion step and a truncation-check step would close both, and both map directly to this run's two MAJOR bugs.

observations: Console/network noise (CSP block on a base64 data:audio resource, a 400 on dctityd.michelinman.com/status-log, 404s on cdn-prod-nam.yepgarage.info network-facet logos) is site-wide background noise present on a clean load with zero test actions - not something this run's actions caused.
The autocomplete-selected results page URL contains a literal comma in its slug (/auto/dealer-locator/atlanta,-ga) - a cosmetic URL-formatting nit, the page itself loads and functions correctly.

The DOM contains a second, entirely visibility:hidden duplicate of the footer/subnav link tree alongside the real visible footer - only the visible one is used by the page; no functional impact observed, but worth a developer's attention as dead markup.
